hazard_consequence_node.label: Jet fire
hazard_consequence_node.name: Jet fire
hazard_consequence_node.evidence: "Very quickly after the mud started spraying out of the well, the diesel oil-based mud and gas escaping the well caught on fire."
hazard_consequence_node.explanation: Within the provided consequence categories, the main hazardous phenomenon is a sustained fire from a pressurized gas/mud release at the well after loss of well control. The report's central analysis is the blowout development, missed influx indications, and failure to shut in the well before ignition, which most closely corresponds to a jet fire rather than an explosion or a brief flash event.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: diesel oil-based mud and gas
entity_nodes.evidence: the diesel oil-based mud and gas escaping the well caught on fire
entity_nodes.explanation: The blowout release that ignited consisted of flammable gas and diesel oil-based drilling mud escaping from the well.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: open well hole on the rig floor
entity_nodes.evidence: open well hole on the rig floor
entity_nodes.explanation: The uncontrolled release emerged from the well opening at the rig floor, where the blowout and immediate fire developed.

condition_nodes.label: Phase
condition_nodes.name: TwoPhase
condition_nodes.evidence: the diesel oil-based mud and gas escaping the well caught on fire
condition_nodes.explanation: The released material included both gas and liquid oil-based mud, indicating a two-phase release.

condition_nodes.label: Pressure
condition_nodes.name: High pressure
condition_nodes.evidence: the pressure on the well side of the orbit valve was previously so high that the trip tank pumps had deadheaded
condition_nodes.explanation: Elevated well pressure existed before the blowout and provided the driving force for the forceful release from the well.

condition_nodes.label: Combustibility
condition_nodes.name: Combustible
condition_nodes.explanation: The released gas and oil-based mud were capable of burning once ignited.

condition_nodes.label: ReleaseType
condition_nodes.name: Continuous release
condition_nodes.evidence: The BOP did not seal the well to stop the blowout
condition_nodes.explanation: The release was sustained as an ongoing blowout rather than a single instantaneous discharge.

condition_nodes.label: Confinement
condition_nodes.name: Low confinement
condition_nodes.evidence: open well hole on the rig floor
condition_nodes.explanation: The release occurred at an open rig-floor location rather than inside a confined enclosure.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Gas influx into the wellbore
event_nodes.explanation: The accident sequence began when gas entered the underbalanced well, initiating the loss-of-well-control progression that led to the blowout.

event_nodes.label: IgnitionSource
event_nodes.name: Unknown ignition source
event_nodes.evidence: the diesel oil-based mud and gas escaping the well caught on fire
event_nodes.explanation: The report clearly states that ignition occurred, but it does not identify the specific ignition source.

event_nodes.label: IntermediateEvent
event_nodes.name: Mud and gas started spraying out of the well
event_nodes.evidence: At 8:36 am, shortly after the driller communicated that he was going to close the blind rams, mud started spraying out of the well.
event_nodes.explanation: The graph currently jumps from gas influx/high pressure directly to the jet fire. The immediate blowout release to atmosphere is the missing physical accident step that directly precedes ignition.
